verdict: JPMorgan earned $16.5B in the quarter — revenue rose 10% to $49.8B on strong trading, dealmaking fees and lending, while credit costs fell by a quarter from a year ago.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 9% on bigger balances (average loans +11% YoY, deposits +7%).

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up 11%, with Markets revenue up 20% and investment banking fees up 31%.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, telecoms and equipment as the bank invests in AI and its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,447M of occupancy) plus other general costs ($1,956M, including $223M of legal expense).

takeaways.title: Returns no rival matches
takeaways.text: Return on tangible common equity hit 23% (19% on common equity) — profitability far beyond what other big banks produce, on $16.5B of net income.

takeaways.title: Dealmaking woke up
takeaways.text: Investment banking fees rose 31% YoY to $2.9B — JPMorgan ranked #1 globally with a 9.8% wallet share — and Markets revenue rose 20%.

takeaways.title: Credit costs fell
takeaways.text: The provision for credit losses fell 24% from a year ago to $2.5B — $2.3B of actual charge-offs plus a small $191M reserve build — even as lending kept growing.

follow100Note: JPMorgan reports revenue two ways: $49.8B reported (GAAP), used here, or $50.5B on a 'managed' basis that grosses up tax-exempt income. Net income is identical either way.
footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $50.5B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $49.8B — the difference is a tax gross-up that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and 'operating profit' here is income before income taxes.
costNodePlain: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid — the provision for credit losses: $2.3B of loans were charged off in the quarter and $191M was added to reserves.
